name: Dermalinfusion

lead: Dermalinfusion pairs skin exfoliation with serum infusion in one pass, offered as a facial to even out skin tone, notably dark marks in skin of color.

A handheld tip exfoliates while delivering a serum to the skin, so pigment-targeting actives reach the surface. The one publication found, a 2014 Journal of Drugs in Dermatology study, combined topical delivery with dermalinfusion of decapeptide-12 to treat post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in skin of color.

paras: It is a clinic facial, with the serum chosen for the skin concern.
No safety information was available in the sources reviewed.

studies.title: Combined topical delivery and dermalinfusion of decapeptide-12 accelerates resolution of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in skin of color.

angle.text: It is used to exfoliate and infuse serums in one pass, notably for dark marks in skin of color, aiming at a more even tone. The research found is a single small 2014 study on post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.

lead: Dermalinfusion is a branded aesthetic procedure that combines a form of exfoliation with simultaneous serum infusion through a handheld tip. Evidence found is limited to one 2014 Journal of Drugs in Dermatology study that combined topical delivery with dermalinfusion of decapeptide-12 to treat post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in skin of color.[1]

paras: A 2014 study reported on combined topical delivery and dermalinfusion of decapeptide-12 for resolving post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in skin of color.[1] No other studies were found.
